headline: Margin expansion and lower deposit costs lift profitability
summary_short: Preliminary Q2 2026 results show diluted EPS of $0.60 (+3.4% y/y, up from $0.55 q/q) as net interest margin expanded 6bps q/q to 3.25% and the cost of deposits fell 2bps to 1.20%, lifting return on average assets to 1.23% and return on average tangible common equity to 16.3%.
summary_long: Net income rose to $73.4M (diluted EPS $0.60), up q/q from $67.8M ($0.55) and 3% y/y, driven by 6bps of net interest margin expansion to 3.25% and a 2bp reduction in cost of deposits to 1.20%. Return on average assets improved 9bps q/q to 1.23%; return on average tangible common equity rose to 16.3% from 15.3%. Gross loans grew to $14.6B from $14.4B q/q. Book value per share rose to $23.22 from $22.75; tangible book value per share reached $15.04, up 3% q/q. Total cash fell 28% y/y to $1,012.5M as shareholders' equity rose 5% y/y to $2,826.0M. Figures are preliminary; First Hawaiian will report final Q2 2026 results on July 24, 2026. No new forward guidance was issued.

drivers.explanation: Company ties the increase to 6bps of net interest margin expansion to 3.25% and a 2bp drop in cost of deposits to 1.20%, which lifted return on average assets and return on tangible common equity.
Growth reflects both the net income increase and a 2.8% y/y reduction in weighted diluted shares outstanding, per our own share-count reconciliation.

Release attributes the quarter's earnings growth to margin expansion, lower deposit costs, higher ROA/ROTCE, and loan growth to $14.6B from $14.4B q/q, alongside a same-day definitive agreement to acquire TriCo Bancshares in an all-stock deal.
